title: Private upgrades: rollback policy + GA gates review (Release Eng / SRE / Security / PM)
summary: Cross-team review of (1) rollback/downgrade policy for Redwood Private upgrades and (2) GA gating criteria. Agreed on a conservative v1 stance: rollback is supported only within a defined window and only when schema migrations are not marked forward-only; otherwise allow abort/pause and require a restore-based recovery path. Security confirmed requirements for offline bundle signature verification and audit events for upgrade/rollback actions. SRE emphasized GA gates around failure-injection coverage, dashboards/alerts, and a support-ready diagnostics bundle. Program agreed to publish a single GA checklist and freeze policy language for beta enablement.
topics: Rollback window definition (time-based vs version-based) and "previous known good" handling
DB migrations policy: forward-only markers, downgrade guardrails, and restore-based recovery
Upgrade orchestration invariants: component ordering, abort vs rollback behaviors, partial upgrade safety
GA gates: precheck coverage, backup verification, telemetry dashboards/alerts, runbook completeness
Security: signed offline bundles, key custody/rotation process, audit logging requirements
questions: Do we define the rollback window as N versions back, or time since upgrade start (e.g., 24h)?
What is the exact operator message when rollback is blocked due to forward-only migrations (and what is the supported recovery path)?
Is GA contingent on automated failure injection in CI, or can some scenarios remain manual with documented drills?
For air-gapped, do we require signature verification on every install/upgrade step or only bundle import?
action_items: Connor O'Brien: update rollback policy doc wording to explicitly separate "abort" vs "rollback" vs "restore" paths; include operator-facing error text for forward-only migrations. Due 2025-01-20.
Michael Nguyen: finalize migration metadata contract (forward-only flag + minimum downgrade version) and share examples for 2 common migration types. Due 2025-01-21.
Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: propose GA thresholds for upgrade-related alerts (failure rate + step-duration anomaly) and confirm dashboard panels required for on-call. Due 2025-01-22.
Marcus Lin / Dr. Aisha Rahman: confirm signing key rotation SOP and what evidence we need for GA (audit events, verification failure behavior). Due 2025-01-23.
Allison Grant: review structured log fields for upgrade correlation id and diagnostics bundle contents for Support intake. Due 2025-01-22.
Talia Benson: publish a single GA checklist page (source of truth) and link to runbook + dashboards + test matrix; align owners and dates. Due 2025-01-24.
next_steps: Talia to circulate notes + decisions and capture remaining open questions as tracked items.
Connor to push updated policy language into Confluence and request async sign-off from SRE + Security.
SRE to validate upgrade rehearsal criteria (go/no-go) for first beta customer window.
Security to confirm offline verification behavior and key rotation process before enabling air-gapped beta.
transcript:
Meeting: Private upgrades — rollback policy + GA gates review (internal)
Recorded: 2025-01-16 17:00 UTC
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Talia Benson, Vivek Kulkarni, Connor O'Brien, Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Marcus Lin, Dr. Aisha Rahman, Sahana Iyer, Allison Grant, Michael Nguyen

---

[00:00] Talia Benson: Alright, top of the hour. Thanks everyone. Goal today is to align on rollback policy language and the GA gates for the Private upgrade/rollback mechanism. I want to leave with decisions, not just “we’ll see.” Connor, you want to frame?

[00:18] Connor O'Brien: Yep. So we’ve got the installer workflow pretty close. The part that keeps coming up in review is “what does rollback mean,” and when do we block it. Second, what’s the actual bar for GA. We’ve got a draft checklist but it’s… a little aspirational.

[00:35] Vivek Kulkarni: Plus customers keep using “rollback” to mean “undo anything that happened,” including data migrations, which we are not going to promise.

[00:44] Sean Gallagher: And on-call keeps using “rollback” as “get service healthy again,” which might mean restore-from-backup and not a literal downgrade.

[00:52] Talia Benson: Exactly. So let’s do (1) definitions, (2) policy decisions, (3) GA gates. Marcus and Aisha, we’ll hit signing and audit too.

[01:03] Marcus Lin: Sounds good.

[01:05] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yep.

[01:06] Talia Benson: Connor, can you state the current invariant assumptions in the upgrade framework?

[01:12] Connor O'Brien: Sure. Current design: upgrade is a step graph. Prechecks first, then backup/snapshot steps, then apply control plane changes, then runtime/gateway, then observability agents. Each step emits structured logs, we have a correlation id. If a step fails, we can either abort (stop, leave as-is), or rollback (re-apply known-good versions + restore snapshot if required). The big caveat is DB migrations: if we ran a forward-only migration, we may block rollback and instead direct to restore or a “forward fix.”

[01:47] Michael Nguyen: Minor nit: forward-only doesn’t always mean “impossible,” but it means we won’t support automated downgrade because the state may not be representable.

[01:57] Vivek Kulkarni: So we should avoid “may.” We should say “rollback is not supported once forward-only migrations are applied.” Deterministic.

[02:06] Sean Gallagher: +1. The “may” is how you get paged at 3 a.m.

[02:10] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s define terms. I’m hearing three: abort, rollback, restore. Can we align?

[02:18] Connor O'Brien: Abort is “stop running steps,” don’t change versions back. Rollback is “actively revert component versions to previous known good,” and optionally restore the control plane DB snapshot if it’s part of the rollback plan. Restore is “rebuild state from backups” — more like disaster recovery.

[02:35] Rafael Mendes: For operator UX, we should say “abort” is safe when you haven’t crossed a rollback-safe boundary. Like before migrations or before the gateway flips traffic.

[02:46] Allison Grant: And from observability: abort should still emit a terminal event. Like upgrade.status=aborted, with reason.

[02:53] Talia Benson: Great. Now the policy doc currently says “supported rollback window: up to previous minor version within 24 hours.” That’s the bit people keep bikeshedding on. Time-based vs version-based.

[03:08] Vivek Kulkarni: From PM: customers ask “can we go from 1.9 back to 1.8.” They don’t ask about hours. So version-based is easier.

[03:16] Sean Gallagher: But time matters because backups expire, and also because if you run for two weeks, your data evolves. Even if schema didn’t change, you’ve got config drift, tokens, whatever.

[03:28] Michael Nguyen: Also, our compatibility matrix is version-based. But migrations are effectively time-based in practice because once you’ve accumulated new rows in a new format, you can’t represent them.

[03:41] Connor O'Brien: Proposal we had in the draft: “Rollback supported to immediately previous known good release (N-1) provided (a) rollback is initiated within 24 hours of upgrade completion and (b) no forward-only migrations have executed.” It’s both.

[03:58] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Can I add a security angle? The longer the window, the more we’re implying we keep old artifacts readily usable. For air-gapped, customers might store them, but we need a policy on how long we sign/verify and how we handle revocations. So shorter is safer.

[04:13] Vivek Kulkarni: I worry 24 hours is too strict for enterprise change windows. They upgrade Friday night, realize an issue Monday.

[04:22] Sean Gallagher: But if they realize Monday, we should be telling them to do a forward fix. Rolling back days later is chaos.

[04:28] Rafael Mendes: Another angle: support needs a crisp playbook. “If within window and no forward-only migration, run rollback command. Else, run restore procedure / escalate.”

[04:40] Talia Benson: What about “business days” type stuff? Eh.

[04:42] Connor O'Brien: We can define it as “within X hours OR before the next scheduled automated backup expiry.” But that’s messy.

[04:52] Michael Nguyen: If we’re snapshotting control plane DB during upgrade, we can set retention. Like keep upgrade snapshots for 7 days, separate from regular backups. That gives you a technical basis.

[05:04] Sean Gallagher: That helps, but doesn’t solve semantic correctness. Even if you can restore, the app might have written data expecting the new version.

[05:13] Vivek Kulkarni: For Private control plane, it’s mostly config/state, not customer app data. But the gateway behavior can differ.

[05:20] Connor O'Brien: Right. The DB is control plane metadata, not user content. That’s why rollback is more feasible, but still not free.

[05:28] Allison Grant: Can we split “control plane rollback” and “runtime rollback”? Like you might revert runtime without touching DB snapshot.

[05:36] Connor O'Brien: We can, but then the operator UX is tricky. Also compatibility matrix may require them together.

[05:43] Sahana Iyer: And CI gates become more complicated if we allow partial. Our step graph assumes ordering.

[05:49] Talia Benson: Let’s land a v1 policy. Vivek wants version-based for customer clarity; Sean wants time-based for safety. Compromise: “N-1 only” plus “recommended within 72 hours” maybe?

[06:03] Sean Gallagher: I can live with 72 instead of 24, if we still block on forward-only migrations.

[06:08] Dr. Aisha Rahman: 72 is fine as long as we don’t promise indefinite artifact availability. For air-gapped they own the artifacts anyway.

[06:15] Marcus Lin: We should also be explicit: for air-gapped, signature verification happens at import and at install/upgrade time. If a key is revoked, older bundles could fail verification. That’s a real operational scenario.

[06:28] Vivek Kulkarni: So language should say “Rollback supported to the immediately previous release within 72 hours, subject to migration constraints and artifact verification.” That’s a mouthful.

[06:39] Talia Benson: We can move verification into “prereqs.” But yes.

[06:43] Connor O'Brien: Another key point: “previous known good” should be defined by the system, not operator guessing. There was a Slack thread about storing it in control plane.

[06:54] Michael Nguyen: We can store last_successful_version in control plane state, updated only after post-upgrade smoke tests pass.

[07:03] Rafael Mendes: That’s huge for on-call. Otherwise you’re looking up Helm releases by hand.

[07:09] Sean Gallagher: And rollback command should refuse to proceed if it can’t identify that version deterministically.

[07:16] Connor O'Brien: Agreed. In current PR, rollback picks previous chart versions from the upgrade plan output. But if someone did a manual hotfix in between, we need drift detection.

[07:29] Allison Grant: Drift detection should show up in diagnostics too: “cluster is not in expected state; these resources differ.”

[07:37] Talia Benson: Okay. Decision 1: rollback supported only to “previous known good version,” defined as last successful upgrade completion + smoke tests. Decision 2: rollback window: 72 hours from upgrade completion. Decision 3: hard block if forward-only migration executed. Any objections?

[07:57] Vivek Kulkarni: No, as long as we are careful in docs that 72 hours is “supported,” not “guaranteed no downtime.”

[08:04] Sean Gallagher: Fine.

[08:05] Marcus Lin: Fine.

[08:06] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Fine.

[08:08] Talia Benson: Great. Now, migrations. Michael, can you explain the forward-only marking in plain language we can put into policy?

[08:16] Michael Nguyen: Yeah. We plan to add a migration metadata table. Each migration has attributes: version introduced, whether it’s reversible, and if there’s a minimum downgrade version. If any applied migration is marked forward-only (or irreversible), automated rollback is blocked. The installer detects that and tells you: rollback not supported; proceed with restore or upgrade-forward remediation.

[08:38] Connor O'Brien: And we should have operator-facing text that’s not scary but clear.

[08:43] Sean Gallagher: It should be scary enough that they don’t try hacks.

[08:45] Vivek Kulkarni: (laughs) “Do not attempt.”

[08:48] Allison Grant: We can include a link to the runbook section in the error. For air-gapped, maybe just a local doc reference.

[08:56] Sahana Iyer: Also we need tests for this behavior. Like a simulated migration flagged forward-only and ensure rollback exits non-zero.

[09:05] Talia Benson: That transitions to GA gates. Let’s list the gates we have now: prechecks coverage, backups verified, rollback hooks, telemetry, diagnostics, signing. Sean, can you describe what SRE considers non-negotiable?

[09:23] Sean Gallagher: Non-negotiable for GA: 
1) Upgrade run emits metrics per step: duration, success/fail, and a top-level status. 
2) Dashboards exist and on-call knows where they are. 
3) Alerting: upgrade failure rate above threshold, and step duration anomaly alert. 
4) Diagnostics bundle: on failure, we can collect precheck report, step logs, k8s events, and some pod logs, without ssh’ing into nodes. 
5) A tested rollback path with target time-to-recover — like restore service health within, say, 30 minutes in our reference env.

[10:02] Rafael Mendes: And runbook is complete enough that a not-the-author can follow it.

[10:06] Vivek Kulkarni: “Not-the-author” is the real gate.

[10:08] Sean Gallagher: Exactly.

[10:10] Talia Benson: Connor, do we have a target for rollback time in PRD?

[10:15] Connor O'Brien: We had “rollback within maintenance window,” which is vague. The integration harness PR had 30 minutes as a target in staging.

[10:24] Sean Gallagher: I’d like us to set something like: P50 rollback time under 20 minutes, P95 under 45, in reference environments. But we can say “best effort” for customer hardware.

[10:37] Vivek Kulkarni: For GA, we can phrase it as internal SLO rather than a customer SLA.

[10:43] Talia Benson: Okay. Marcus/Aisha: Security gates.

[10:47] Marcus Lin: For GA: 
- Signed artifacts: installer verifies signatures for upgrade bundles (especially offline). If verification fails, it must fail closed.
- Audit logging: control plane records upgrade/rollback actions: who/what/when/version/correlation id. 
- Secrets handling: backups shouldn’t dump secrets in plaintext into diagnostics. Redaction rules.

[11:09] Dr. Aisha Rahman: And we need a documented key custody and rotation process. Doesn’t have to be perfect automation v1, but it must exist. Also policy on what happens if a signing key is compromised: how we revoke, and how customers get new bundles.

[11:26] Allison Grant: On diagnostics, we can do a “support bundle” with a redaction pass. But we need to be careful: k8s events sometimes include env var snippets.

[11:36] Rafael Mendes: We’ve seen that. Some clusters log secrets-ish stuff in events from misconfigured charts.

[11:41] Connor O'Brien: We can scope diagnostics to: recent pod logs for specific namespaces and only last N lines; and avoid dumping full manifests.

[11:52] Sean Gallagher: But then support will ask for the manifests.

[11:55] Vivek Kulkarni: Could make it opt-in flag: “--include-manifests” with warning.

[12:02] Marcus Lin: That’s acceptable as long as default is safe and we log that operator chose to include it.

[12:08] Talia Benson: Good. That’s an action item for Allison to review the log fields + redaction.

[12:14] Sahana Iyer: On the GA gate about failure injection: do we require it all automated in CI? Some scenarios like “disk full” are hard.

[12:24] Sean Gallagher: We don’t need 100% automated, but we do need a documented drill and at least a subset automated. Especially: image pull failure, API unavailable, schema mismatch, permissions missing.

[12:36] Connor O'Brien: The current harness can simulate mid-upgrade failure by killing a job and messing with a chart hook. Disk full is… we can do a fake threshold by setting free space precheck to a high value.

[12:48] Michael Nguyen: Schema mismatch is the big one. We should test the downgrade guard: if migration metadata indicates forward-only, rollback blocked.

[12:57] Vivek Kulkarni: That’s also the policy we’ll get grilled on by enterprise prospects.

[13:03] Dr. Aisha Rahman: On that note, the language should not be “we’ll try.” It should be “not supported; here is the supported recovery.”

[13:10] Talia Benson: Yes. “Supported recovery” means restore-from-snapshot and re-apply current version, right?

[13:17] Sean Gallagher: Most likely. Or deploy a hotfix forward. But minimum: restore control plane DB to pre-upgrade snapshot and then reinstall last known good stack. That’s basically rollback-plus-restore.

[13:29] Connor O'Brien: The nuance: if migrations are forward-only, restoring DB snapshot might revert metadata, but the runtime might have already moved. We need ordering guidance.

[13:39] Rafael Mendes: That’s runbook material: “If rollback blocked, do not downgrade components. Escalate to support; use restore procedure.”

[13:47] Talia Benson: Let’s move to operator UX. There was debate on interactive prompts vs flags. Connor?

[13:55] Connor O'Brien: Current CLI has interactive prompts by default for rollback because it’s dangerous. But Support asked for non-interactive mode for automation. We added flags like --yes and --non-interactive.

[14:10] Sean Gallagher: As long as prompts don’t hide critical info. The prompt should show what it’s about to do: restore snapshot ID, target versions, expected downtime.

[14:19] Allison Grant: And print the correlation id early so logs can be matched.

[14:23] Marcus Lin: Also, in non-interactive mode, it still needs a clear audit event: operator initiated rollback with non-interactive flag.

[14:31] Vivek Kulkarni: For docs, we should show both: “human” path and “automation” path.

[14:36] Talia Benson: Okay. Now GA gates list. I’m going to read what I have in my notes and you tell me if missing:
- Precheck framework with severity + remediation hints, JSON output for Support ingestion
- Backup primitive with verification step and retention guidance
- Upgrade step graph with health gates and deterministic ordering
- Rollback command with guardrails (migration checks, drift detection)
- Offline bundle import + signature verification for air-gapped
- Telemetry: structured logs + metrics + dashboards + alerts
- Diagnostics bundle with redaction defaults
- Runbook + support escalation path + change management doc
- Automated test plan / failure injection matrix with minimum coverage

[15:21] Sean Gallagher: Add “post-upgrade smoke test” is required and should be part of upgrade completion criteria.

[15:27] Connor O'Brien: Yes. In helm charts we have a post-upgrade job. If it fails, upgrade should be marked failed and rollback offered.

[15:36] Michael Nguyen: And for DB migrations, we should have a “migration dry run check” maybe? At least “schema compatibility precheck” to detect incompatible versions.

[15:46] Sahana Iyer: That’s in prechecks spec but we haven’t fully implemented.

[15:50] Vivek Kulkarni: For GA, can it be “implemented for common DB types” and documented limitations?

[15:56] Sean Gallagher: Sure, but don’t ship with “TODO.” If it’s not implemented, we say it’s not supported.

[16:04] Marcus Lin: Another security gate: make sure upgrade actions are tied to an identity. For Private, sometimes it’s just “whoever has kubeconfig.” We at least need the installer to record operator-provided identity string (name/email) in audit event.

[16:20] Connor O'Brien: We can require --operator or read from env var, and it ends up in audit. It’s not perfect but better.

[16:29] Dr. Aisha Rahman: For GA, that’s acceptable as a baseline. Long term we want SSO/identity integration, but that’s out of scope.

[16:38] Talia Benson: Great. Another question: do we gate GA on “key rotation process doc” completion? Sounds like yes.

[16:45] Marcus Lin: Yes.

[16:46] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes.

[16:47] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s talk about the biggest risk: partial upgrades leaving the system unrecoverable. Sean, what scenarios worry you most?

[17:00] Sean Gallagher: Anything that flips traffic before control plane is stable. Example: gateway rollout starts, but control plane API is still migrating. Then you get 502s and retries. The ordering gate must be strict.

[17:14] Connor O'Brien: We added a readiness gate to prevent that exact edge case. Gateway waits until control plane health endpoint reports ready and versions match.

[17:23] Rafael Mendes: Also the “observability agent” is lower risk. It should never block upgrade completion.

[17:29] Allison Grant: It can block if you misconfigure it, but I agree it should be best-effort. We shouldn’t roll back an entire upgrade because the dashboard agent didn’t install.

[17:39] Vivek Kulkarni: That’s a policy decision: component criticality levels.

[17:43] Connor O'Brien: In the step graph, we have “required” vs “optional” steps. Optional failures mark upgrade “degraded” but not failed.

[17:53] Sean Gallagher: I want SRE sign-off on which are optional.

[17:56] Talia Benson: Capture as GA checklist item: “criticality classification signed off by SRE.”

[18:03] Sahana Iyer: Another gate: compatibility matrix enforcement. Quentin owns it but he’s not here. Installer must block unsupported version jumps.

[18:12] Connor O'Brien: Yep. Currently upgrade plan validates you’re not skipping beyond supported minor versions. Also checks control plane/runtime/chart skew rules.

[18:23] Michael Nguyen: And it must incorporate migration constraints. If migration requires intermediate step, it should enforce that.

[18:31] Talia Benson: Okay. Let’s talk about air-gapped specifically. Marcus, what’s the required operator workflow?

[18:38] Marcus Lin: Operator receives an offline bundle. They run “bundle import” which validates manifest and signature. Then upgrade uses only artifacts in local cache. Verification should happen at import time and ideally again at use time to ensure cache wasn’t tampered.

[18:56] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Also we should document what happens when verification fails: exact error, where to look, and what support needs (hashes, manifest, etc.).

[19:07] Connor O'Brien: The CLI prints “SIGNATURE_INVALID” with details and exits. We can add guidance: “Do not proceed; contact Redwood Support; include bundle manifest and sha256.”

[19:19] Allison Grant: We should ensure those errors end up in diagnostics bundle too.

[19:23] Rafael Mendes: For air-gapped, support can’t get the bundle unless customer shares it. So we should ask for the manifest only.

[19:31] Marcus Lin: Good point.

[19:33] Talia Benson: Now, open questions: time window is 72 hours, N-1. We’ve decided that. What about “rollback auto-trigger”? Like if upgrade fails, do we auto-rollback?

[19:47] Sean Gallagher: No auto by default. Too risky. But we can present a recommended next action.

[19:52] Connor O'Brien: The framework supports auto-rollback, but we left it off. Some customers may want it in the future.

[19:59] Vivek Kulkarni: For v1, manual with clear guidance is fine.

[20:03] Rafael Mendes: On-call prefers manual. Auto rollback can mask the root cause and thrash.

[20:10] Talia Benson: Okay. Another: maintenance window guidance. Vivek, what do we want to say?

[20:18] Vivek Kulkarni: We should recommend a window based on environment size. But we can’t predict. So we’ll give ranges from our tests: small cluster ~20-30 min, medium ~45-60. And call out backups can dominate.

[20:33] Sean Gallagher: And say “do a rehearsal in staging with same size.”

[20:37] Connor O'Brien: The runbook already says “practice run.” We can make it more prominent.

[20:42] Sahana Iyer: GA gate: first end-to-end rehearsal in staging must pass with go/no-go criteria. That was in the release thread.

[20:52] Talia Benson: Yep. We’ll add it.

[20:55] Allison Grant: Quick note: metrics naming. Right now it’s like upgrade_step_duration_seconds with labels step_name, result. That’s good. But we need correlation id for logs, not metrics.

[21:07] Sean Gallagher: Yes, metrics shouldn’t explode cardinality.

[21:10] Allison Grant: Exactly. Logs will have correlation id.

[21:14] Talia Benson: Let’s spend 5 minutes on “what does GA mean.” Is GA enabling this for all Private customers, or just VPC? On-prem is harder.

[21:25] Vivek Kulkarni: PM stance: GA for VPC first, then on-prem GA later. But we can do “air-gapped beta” concurrently.

[21:33] Connor O'Brien: From eng: the same mechanism works; the difference is bundle import and signing. That’s the gating item.

[21:41] Marcus Lin: I’m okay with GA for VPC first. For on-prem GA, security wants evidence that bundle verification is working and rotation SOP is in place.

[21:50] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. And we should have at least one on-prem pilot before we call it GA.

[21:57] Talia Benson: So “GA” in the checklist should be explicit: GA-VPC and GA-OnPrem. Two tracks.

[22:04] Sean Gallagher: SRE also wants at least one real-world beta upgrade with a customer before GA. Staging-only is not enough.

[22:12] Vivek Kulkarni: That’s in the PRD: 1-2 beta customers.

[22:16] Talia Benson: Great. Next: how we communicate downgrade limitations. Vivek, have you seen common misunderstandings?

[22:25] Vivek Kulkarni: Yes. People assume “downgrade” is always possible. We need to say “downgrade is not the default; rollback is constrained; forward-only migrations block downgrade.” Also emphasize: “No promise of zero downtime.”

[22:41] Sean Gallagher: Put it in bold in docs. Seriously.

[22:44] Connor O'Brien: Also in CLI error messages. Like if you try to rollback and it’s blocked, we show why and what to do.

[22:52] Michael Nguyen: We should standardize error codes. Support will ask.

[22:56] Allison Grant: Error codes can be in logs and JSON output.

[23:00] Sahana Iyer: Then we can write tests around them.

[23:03] Talia Benson: Okay. We’re converging. Let’s do rapid-fire decisions:

[23:08] Talia Benson: 1) Auto rollback default off. Everyone?

[23:11] All: (general agreement)

[23:12] Talia Benson: 2) Rollback to N-1 previous known good only, within 72 hours, blocked if forward-only migrations executed.

[23:21] All: (agreement)

[23:22] Talia Benson: 3) GA is split: GA-VPC and GA-OnPrem; OnPrem requires at least one pilot and signing rotation SOP.

[23:33] Marcus Lin: Yes.

[23:34] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes.

[23:35] Sean Gallagher: Yes.

[23:36] Vivek Kulkarni: Yes.

[23:37] Talia Benson: Great. Now, open items: 
- Connor to update policy doc language + operator messages.
- Michael to finalize migration metadata contract.
- Sean/Rafael to propose alert thresholds and panels.
- Marcus/Aisha to confirm key rotation SOP.
- Allison to confirm log fields and diagnostics redaction defaults.
- I’ll publish a single GA checklist.

[24:05] Connor O'Brien: One more nuance: “previous known good” for first install? Like if you’re upgrading from a version that didn’t have the metadata.

[24:14] Michael Nguyen: If old version doesn’t report, we can derive from Helm release history but less reliable.

[24:19] Sean Gallagher: That should be “best effort,” not GA requirement.

[24:23] Vivek Kulkarni: For existing installs, we’ll have a migration to create the metadata. But chicken-and-egg.

[24:31] Connor O'Brien: We can do: if metadata missing, rollback requires explicit --target-version, with extra warnings.

[24:39] Marcus Lin: That’s okay as long as we log it.

[24:41] Talia Benson: Let’s add as a doc caveat. Not a blocker.

[24:46] Allison Grant: Also, we should ensure “upgrade correlation id” is propagated into control plane logs. I think there’s a PR but it’s not fully rolled out.

[24:56] Connor O'Brien: Yep, it’s in review. We’ll mark it as GA gate for telemetry traceability.

[25:02] Sean Gallagher: Without that, triage is painful.

[25:05] Talia Benson: Good catch.

[25:07] Vivek Kulkarni: Another question: what’s the customer-facing promise on “downtime minimized with safe sequencing/canaries.” How do we reflect that?

[25:18] Sean Gallagher: We can say we do readiness gates and component ordering, but we won’t claim zero downtime. Also, canary for control plane is tricky in Private.

[25:29] Connor O'Brien: For runtime, we can do rolling updates; for control plane, we do one-at-a-time with health checks.

[25:38] Rafael Mendes: The runbook should tell them what to monitor: gateway error rate, control plane readiness, job statuses.

[25:45] Talia Benson: Okay. Anything else on GA gates before we wrap?

[25:51] Marcus Lin: Just to reiterate: fail closed on signature verification. No “--ignore-signature” escape hatch.

[25:58] Connor O'Brien: There’s no ignore flag. We considered one for dev, but we can keep it hidden behind a build tag.

[26:05] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please keep it out of customer builds.

[26:08] Connor O'Brien: Yes.

[26:10] Sahana Iyer: For release train, do we ship this behind a feature flag for beta?

[26:16] Vivek Kulkarni: Yes. Beta enablement per customer.

[26:20] Sean Gallagher: And SRE wants a runbook section for “how to enable/disable feature flag” and what telemetry to check.

[26:27] Allison Grant: We can add a dashboard filter “upgrade_feature_enabled=true” if we tag customers, but that might be too much.

[26:34] Talia Benson: We can do that later. For beta, manual tracking is okay but error-prone.
